review_cost.rationale: One round of changes before approving: 404/error handling, route typing, and the home-route revalidation strategy; the rest is solid enough to merge with nits.

findings.issue: 404s are returned as { notFound: true } and rendered inline (same in move.tsx:6, ability.tsx:6, type-detail.tsx:6); the framework's documented pattern is to throw a 404 Response/data() and render a route ErrorBoundary, which also gives the HTTP 404 the spec encourages.
findings.suggestion: In each loader, `throw data("Not Found", { status: 404 })` and render one shared ErrorBoundary that shows the Not found UI; keep the splat route for unknown paths.

findings.issue: No ErrorBoundary is exported anywhere; a thrown fetch error (API 500/network) from api.server.ts:35 leaves the user on the framework's default error screen.
findings.suggestion: Add a root ErrorBoundary with a friendly fallback and a link home; add route-level ones where useful.

findings.issue: Each keystroke navigates via setSearchParams, revalidating the loader and re-serializing the full 1025-species HomeData (~200KB) to the client per keystroke.
findings.suggestion: Either parse q/type/generation/page in the loader (framework-recommended) so payloads stay page-sized, or add `shouldRevalidate` to skip refetching when only search params change (the dataset is cached server-side anyway).

findings.issue: loader, meta and component args are typed `any` (also move.tsx:5-20, ability.tsx, type-detail.tsx), bypassing the framework's generated route types.
findings.suggestion: Use `Route.LoaderArgs`, `Route.MetaArgs` and `Route.ComponentProps` from ./+types/<route> (or at least `typegen`-typed interfaces), and move the inferred-loaderData pattern already used in home.tsx/types.tsx everywhere.

findings.issue: Single 500+ line god data module: response cache, five module-scope index promises and all per-page mappers live together; any page change touches this file.
findings.suggestion: Keep the fetch/cache core and shared indexes, but split per-page mapping (home, pokemon, move, ability, type) into their own modules or colocate the mapping in each route's loader.

findings.issue: Top-level IIFE promises eagerly fire requests at import time; a startup API failure rejects before any loader awaits them (unhandled-rejection risk) and the results cache forever with no invalidation.
findings.suggestion: Wrap in lazily-initialised memoised functions (like getHomeData already is) with a `.catch` guard, so failures surface through loaders/Route error handling.

findings.issue: Two URL-update idioms on the same page: select filters use setSearchParams while pagination builds query strings by hand into `/?...`.
findings.suggestion: Build pagination hrefs with a single param-helper (or use setSearchParams-free `<Link>` built from the same helper used by navigateWithParam) to keep param encoding in one place.

findings.issue: Home route meta returns the same 'Pokédex' title as the root meta (app/root.tsx:17-19); redundant duplication of the default.
findings.suggestion: Delete the home meta export and rely on the root's title.

findings.issue: Generation options are emitted in raw API list order with no explicit ordering field, so 'Generation I … IX in that order' depends on the API's list order holding.
findings.suggestion: Sort generation infos by `record.id` (or a generation ordinal) before exposing them.

findings.issue: Search state sync via previousQ ref plus a document.activeElement guard is subtle: back/forward while the input is focused leaves the visible query desynced from the URL.
findings.suggestion: Add a brief comment explaining the guard, or drive the input value from searchParams with a small controlled-state helper (e.g. React's useFormState/useOptimistic-style or a tiny custom hook) so the URL is the single source of truth.

summary: A competent, genuinely framework-mode React Router app on the current stable version with correct routing, careful URL state, and clean server-only data boundaries. The main gaps are the hand-rolled 404 sentinel pattern instead of thrown 404s plus ErrorBoundaries, pervasive `any` where generated route types exist, and a home page that re-serializes the whole dataset to the client on every keystroke. I'd ask for one round of changes before merging, but nothing structural needs rework.
